answer: An island's terrace farms buy measurements of a volcanic plume. Pay agents only for fresh readings signed by sensors with manufacturer-certified, nonexportable keys. Give each certified device one reward quota per epoch, shared across every agent citing it, and reject reused challenge nonces. A thousand software identities using one sensor cannot multiply its quota; scaling the attack requires buying and deploying more certified hardware. A compromised certifier defeats this limit, and honest agents without hardware face an access barrier.
